newsitem.title: INDIA: Cricket - South Africa cruise into Titan Cup final.
newsitem.headline: Cricket - South Africa cruise into Titan Cup final.

text.p: South Africa, already assured of a place in the final, crushed Australia by eight wicket in the Titan Cup triangular series on Friday.
An unbeaten 88 by Lance Kluesner helped them to their third successive win over the Australians with five overs to spare.
Australia's 50-over total of 238 for six was never likely to be enough after Kluesner and opener Andrew Hudson had put on 73 off 76 balls for the second wicket.
South Africa's opponents in the November 6 final in Bombay will be decided by Sunday's last league match between Australia and India in the northern city of Mohali.
Victory for India would put the hosts in the final but an Australian win would leave the two teams level on points. Superior run rate would then come into play.
Hudson and Gary Kirsten established a solid base to the South African innings with an opening stand of 60. Hudson, who scored 65 from 85 balls, and Kluesner then accelerated the run rate.
Their entertaining stand was broken when Hudson swept Stuart Law to Brad Hogg at backward square-leg.
Kluesner and Darryl Cullinan, who hit an unbeaten 43, profited from some loose bowling with a century third-wicket stand to carry their side to a comfortable victory.
Australia's total was built around Michael Bevan's 79 and Michael Slater's unbeaten 53.
"We did not bowl well and allowed the batsmen to pick up runs with ease," said Australian captain Mark Taylor. "But don't write us off yet."
